clue.text: Goes over river expanse capsizing

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned over, so the word for expanse is read backwards

parts.note: an expanse is a stretch of open space

explanation.surface: A boat crosses a wide stretch of river and overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes over' looks like crossing the river, but means reviews; 'capsizing' gives ECAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going over the main points once more.

clue.text: Artist's style almost becoming rogue

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist, plus the S

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to style someone is to call them a name

explanation.surface: A painter's manner turning roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous person or scoundrel, so a rogue.

clue.text: Understood criminal's genuine, touching judge's heart

parts.note: a con is a convict, plus the S
genuine means true

indicators.note: the heart of the word judge is its central letter

explanation.surface: A villain's honesty is seen to move the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Construed means interpreted, how something was understood.

clue.text: Vegetable crop is below standard

indicators.note: in a down answer the crop word sits below the standard

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
to crop is to snip or cut short

explanation.surface: A vegetable harvest is poorer than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable.

clue.text: Heckles a bishop in seconds

indicators.note: the article and the bishop go inside the word for seconds

parts.note: to second someone is to back them, so seconds are backs
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman is jeered at within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: ARR goes in after the first letter of BACKS. 'seconds' is a verb here, as in seconding a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack, mainly British usage, is to jeer at or shout down a speaker.

clue.text: Queen about to lift port by the Med

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting reads the letters upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A queen has an outing to a Mediterranean harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient harbour city in northern Israel on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Most optimistic with one's love rising during sleep

indicators.note: during puts these letters within the sleep word

parts.note: rest is sleep

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful dreams of their beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ISO into OSI, which goes inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosy means hopeful, so the superlative means most hopeful.

clue.text: Battle on board revolutionary ship

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's usual revolutionary
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A fight aboard a mutinous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means on a chessboard, not aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a war game, a contest of armies played on a board.

clue.text: Uncertainty of Sun's leader writers in employ

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
the writers go inside the employ word

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
pens are writing tools

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper's editorial uncertain about hiring journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial, but is just the first letter of Sun's.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty about what will happen.

clue.text: Guard dispatched by railway

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent off

explanation.surface: A guard is sent off by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard.

clue.text: City over in Europe's less urbanised

indicators.note: over tells us the hidden letters are turned back to front
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A city is said to be less built-up than the rest of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SLESSURB, spanning Europe's, less and urbanised, is read backwards because of 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is the Belgian capital and seat of EU institutions, so a city.

clue.text: Confound, so a hint's in order

indicators.note: put in order means these letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone baffled is told a clue has been set out neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound someone is to amaze or bewilder them, a synonym.

clue.text: Sniffs out small change in France

parts.note: French coins are euro cents

explanation.surface: Someone detects a few coins lying about in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to detect it by smell, to sniff it out.

clue.text: Tenant not so level periodically

parts.note: not so much is less

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of the word level

explanation.surface: A tenant is described as less even than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, so is a tenant.

clue.text: The French fever for Union

parts.note: le is French for the
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A French union suffering from fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or association, a union.

clue.text: Simple routine upset about including new start

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around
the start of new is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A simple routine is disrupted by a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles ROUTINE, UPSET and N together; 'upset' is fodder, though it looks like the anagram signal, and 'including' just adds the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpretentious is modest and plain, without airs, so simple.

clue.text: Upset seeing husband in public squabble

indicators.note: the husband goes in between the words for public and squabble

parts.note: overt means open, public
a row is a squabble

explanation.surface: Someone upset sees a husband in a public argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset is to overturn or overthrow, as in toppling a regime.

clue.text: Fell embracing fabulous creature getting separated

indicators.note: embracing means holding the creature inside

parts.note: fell means dropped or dived
an orc is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: A couple falling for a monster ends up split.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorced couple has legally separated.

clue.text: Tireless debating if ale is drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Debaters keep going tirelessly as long as there's beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable means unable to be wearied, so tireless.

clue.text: Bolts securing practically ancient buildings

indicators.note: securing holds the shortened word inside

parts.note: to bolt is to flee, to fly

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: Bolts holding up ancient buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Follies are extravagant decorative buildings with no real purpose.

clue.text: Simpler to accept this compiler's turning crazier

indicators.note: to accept means the word holds the turned letters

parts.note: barer means more plain, simpler

indicators.note: turning reads the two letters backwards

parts.note: this compiler is I, and the 's adds AM, giving I'M

explanation.surface: A setter admits that things become crazier.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is British slang for crazy. 'this compiler's' stands for I'M, which 'turning' makes MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is a British word for mad, so barmier means more crazy.

clue.text: Southern church concealing fringe programme

indicators.note: concealing holds the fringe word inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is the edge or fringe of cloth

explanation.surface: A church in the south hides a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan, a programme.

clue.text: Authority of old people holding line

indicators.note: the people word holds the line inside it

parts.note: a people or nation can be called a race

explanation.surface: An authority figure from elderly people keeps to the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a source of wise, authoritative pronouncement, an authority.

clue.text: Provokes having first cut relations

indicators.note: having first cut means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: to taunt is to provoke

explanation.surface: Provocation leads to severing family ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, so relations.

clue.text: Name jerk admitting single currency is unstable

indicators.note: admitting means letting the currency inside

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
the euro is Europe's single currency

explanation.surface: Someone shaky is named as a fool for letting in the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes someone emotionally anxious and erratic, so unstable.

clue.text: Nude apart from last item of costume

parts.note: bar means except, apart from

indicators.note: last item means the final letter of costume

explanation.surface: Naked except for the final piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means naked, unclothed.

clue.text: One dines on one's own!

parts.note: seemingly a solo diner, but one who eats their own kind

explanation.surface: Someone eats alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one's own' looks like 'alone', but means feeding on fellow humans.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats flesh of its own species, literally dining on its own kind.

clue.text: Bore in scrap round end of bar

indicators.note: the piece word goes round the final letter

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of bar

explanation.surface: A tedious person scraps around closing time in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is a verb here, to drill through.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to drill through, to make a hole in, synonym.

clue.text: Blow from wind is astern

indicators.note: from tells us the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gale coming from behind a ship, with nautical air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' and 'wind' suggest weather, but Blow is a setback and the letters run through wind is astern.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a sudden misfortune or calamity, a disaster.

clue.text: Begin reading only without serious effort initially

definitions.text: Begin reading only without serious effort initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Starting a book just by flicking casually through its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: to browse is to dip into reading without serious effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Browsing means looking through text casually without a sustained effort.
